361496.title: Equivalence conjecture for amoeba immortality notions
361496.statement:
Let $A$=(H,m) be an amoeba. An amoeba is **immortal** if it admits an infinite growth sequence, **strongly immortal** if every relevant growth process can continue indefinitely, and **partially immortal** if there is an infinite growth sequence from some starting configuration.

**Immortality-equivalence conjecture.** The following properties of an amoeba $A$ are equivalent:

- $A$ is immortal.
- $A$ is strongly immortal.
- $A$ is partially immortal.

In general, strong immortality implies immortality, while the converse is open; for extension parameters $\ell\in\{1,2\}$ the converse is known. The conjecture would identify the three notions of immortality, leaving no distinction between them.

361534.title: Zero-freeness transfer to a neighborhood of zero for 2-spin systems
361534.statement: Fix parameters $\beta$ and $\gamma$, not both zero, and let $Z^{\sigma_\Lambda}_{G}(\lambda)$ denote the partition function of the 2-spin system with boundary condition $\sigma_\Lambda$. Suppose it is zero-free on a complex region $U$. **Zero-freeness transfer conjecture.** There exists a complex neighborhood $U'$ of $0$ such that $U\subseteq U'$ and $Z^{\sigma_\Lambda}_{G}(\lambda)$ is zero-free on $U'$. The paper asks whether all zero-free regions for 2-spin systems must arise in complex neighborhoods of $\lambda=0$ or, after a spin switch, from the other special parameter setting. This remains open in the source.

361695.title: Ge–Li–Lu–Zhou even-eigenvalue-sum conjecture
361695.statement:
Let $T_X:M(n,\mathbb{C})\to M(n,\mathbb{C})$ be defined by $T_X(Y)=[X^*,[X,Y]]$, and let $\lambda_1(T_X)\geq\cdots\geq\lambda_N(T_X)$ be its eigenvalues. **Ge–Li–Lu–Zhou conjecture.** For $\mathbb{K}=\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{K}=\mathbb{C}$, if $X\in M(n,\mathbb{K})$ and $\|X\|=1$, then

$$
\sum_{i=1}^{2k}\lambda_i(T_X)\leq 2k+2,\qquad k=1,\ldots,\left\lfloor\frac{n^2}{2}\right\rfloor.
$$

This is presented as an equivalent form of the fundamental Lu–Wenzel conjecture, and the supplied text gives no independent resolution status.

361746.title: Soft polyhedric realization conjecture for balanced normal convex tilings
361746.statement:
Let $M$ be a balanced, normal, convex tiling.

**Soft polyhedric realization conjecture.** There exists a combinatorially equivalent, soft polyhedric tiling $M'$.

Theorem 1 proves this conclusion under the stronger assumption that every dual of a vertex polyhedron in $M$ has a Hamiltonian circuit. The source suggests that this sufficient condition may be relaxable, but does not establish the conjecture in general.

361806.title: Uniqueness of triangle colours within components of the 2-coloured flip graph
361806.statement: Let $P_{n+2}$ be a convex polygon, and consider its $2$-coloured flip graph, whose vertices are triangulations with triangles coloured using two colours. A triangle is understood by its three vertices and its position in the polygon. **The triangle-position uniqueness conjecture.** In any connected component of the $2$-coloured flip graph, a triangle cannot appear in the same position with different colours. The authors observed this in the examples they considered, including components displayed for polygons with $n=6$ and $n=7$, but the supplied text gives no proof or resolution.

361837.title: Unbounded magnitude conjecture for the triangular-number Möbius function
361837.statement:
Let $\mathcal T(i)=\frac12 i(i+1)$ be the $i$-th triangular number, let $i\leq_{\mathcal T}j$ mean that $\mathcal T(i)$ divides $\mathcal T(j)$, and let $\mu_{\mathcal T}$ be the Möbius function of the poset $(\mathbb N,\leq_{\mathcal T})$. **Unbounded magnitude conjecture.** For any positive integer $M$, there is a positive integer $n$ such that

$$
|\mu_{\mathcal T}(n)|\geq M.
$$

This formalizes the empirical observation that the triangular-number Möbius values attain arbitrarily large magnitude, in contrast with the classical Möbius function; no resolution is supplied.

361903.title: Pach–Saghafian–Schnider lower-bound conjecture for plane star-forest decompositions
361903.statement:
A **complete geometric graph** is a complete graph drawn with vertices in general position and straight-line edges. A **plane $k$-star-forest** is a star-forest with at most $k$ connected components. **Pach–Saghafian–Schnider's conjecture.** The number of plane $k$-star-forests needed to decompose a complete geometric graph on $n$ vertices is at least

$$
\frac{(k+1)n}{2k}.
$$

This conjecture concerns the variant in which each star-forest is required to have at most $k$ components; the source gives no resolution, so the lower bound remains open.

361912.title: The wall-subdivision formulation of the induced-grid conjecture
361912.statement: Let $d$ be a positive integer and let $\mathcal{C}$ be a hereditary graph class excluding $K_{1,d}$. A **subdivision of the elementary $k$-wall** is obtained by subdividing edges of the elementary $k$-wall, and its line graph is formed by taking edges as vertices. **The wall-subdivision formulation.** The class $\mathcal{C}$ has bounded tree-independence number if and only if there exists a positive integer $k$ such that $\mathcal{C}$ excludes all subdivisions of the elementary $k$-wall and their line graphs. This is stated as an equivalent induced-subgraph formulation of the induced-grid conjecture and remains open with that conjecture.

362097.title: The four locally irregular subgraphs conjecture
362097.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a connected graph, and let $\mathfrak{T}'$ be the family of connected graphs that are not decomposable into any number of locally irregular subgraphs. A graph is **decomposable** into $k$ locally irregular subgraphs if its edge set can be partitioned as $E=E_1\cup\cdots\cup E_k$ so that each spanning subgraph $(V,E_i)$ is locally irregular, meaning that adjacent vertices have distinct degrees.

**Four-subgraph conjecture.** Each connected graph $G$ which does not belong to $\mathfrak{T}'$ is decomposable to $4$ locally irregular subgraphs.

This is the less restrictive variant proposed after a connected exception to the three-subgraph conjecture was found. The source does not state a resolution of this four-subgraph variant.

362129.title: Wong and Zhu's $(1,3)$-choosability conjecture for graphs without isolated edges
362129.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. A total-weight assignment is a proper assignment of real weights to the vertices and edges of $G$ such that the sums of incident edge weights and the vertex weight differ on every adjacent pair. The graph is **$(k,k')$-choosable** if every list assignment with lists of size $k$ on vertices and $k'$ on edges admits a proper total weighting from the lists.

**Wong and Zhu's conjecture.** Every graph with no isolated edges is $(1,3)$-choosable.

This is one of the list total-weighting conjectures proposed by Wong and Zhu; its resolution is not specified in the source.

362134.title: The equivariant classification conjecture for graph $C^*$-algebras
362134.statement:
Let $E$ and $F$ be finite graphs, and let $C^*(E)$ and $C^*(F)$ be their graph $C^*$-algebras with gauge circle actions. Let $K^{\mathbb T}_0$ denote equivariant $K$-theory, viewed as an ordered $\mathbb Z[x,x^{-1}]$-module.

**Equivariant classification conjecture.** There is an order-preserving $\mathbb Z[x,x^{-1}]$-module isomorphism

$$
\phi:K^{\mathbb T}_0(C^*(E))\to K^{\mathbb T}_0(C^*(F)),
$$

with $\phi([C^*(E)])=[C^*(F)]$, if and only if $C^*(E)$ and $C^*(F)$ are isomorphic by an isomorphism respecting the gauge action.

This is the analytic counterpart of the graded classification conjecture for Leavitt path algebras, using the identification between graded and equivariant $K$-theory. The source gives no resolution status.

362201.title: Conjecture on Fano planes in non-classical unitals of even order
362201.statement:
Let $q$ be even, let ${\mathcal U}$ be a non-classical unital in ${\operatorname{PG}}(2,q^2)$, and let a **Fano plane** mean an embedded projective plane of order $2$.

**Fano-plane conjecture.** Every non-classical unital ${\mathcal U}$ in ${\operatorname{PG}}(2,q^2)$ contains a Fano plane if $q\geq 4$.

The paper proves the existence of Fano planes in orthogonal Buekenhout--Metz unitals of even order, providing evidence for this broader claim about non-classical unitals. The supplied material gives no resolution of the conjecture in general.

371633.title: The product dimension conjecture for posets
371633.statement:
Let $P$ and $Q$ be posets. Write $P\times Q$ for their Cartesian product, ordered componentwise, and let $\dim(P)$ denote the least integer $n$ such that $P$ is isomorphic to a subposet of $(\mathbb{R}^n,\leq)$. **The product dimension conjecture.**

$$
\dim(P\times Q)\geq \dim(P)+\dim(Q)-2.
$$

This is described as a long-standing conjecture in order-dimension theory; the supplied text gives no resolution, so its status is open.

371682.title: The acyclic 3-dicolouring conjecture for planar oriented graphs
371682.statement:
An **oriented planar graph** is an orientation of a planar graph without a pair of opposite arcs. For an oriented graph $D$, let $\vec{\chi}_{\rm a}(D)$ denote the least number of colours in a vertex-colouring whose monochromatic subdigraphs are acyclic.

**Planar acyclic dichromatic conjecture.** Every oriented planar graph $D$ satisfies

$$
\vec{\chi}_{\rm a}(D)\leq3.
$$

The paper proves the upper bound $5$ and gives a planar oriented graph with acyclic dichromatic number at least $3$. Thus the conjectured bound would be tight if true, but its validity remains open.

371702.title: Katznelson's negative answer conjecture for Bohr and topological recurrence
371702.statement:
A set $S\subset\mathbb{N}$ is a **set of Bohr recurrence** if it meets every Bohr set, and a **set of topological recurrence** if it is a set of topological recurrence in the dynamical sense.

**Katznelson's conjecture.** There is a set $S\subset\mathbb{N}$ which is a set of Bohr recurrence but not a set of topological recurrence.

This is the negative answer to Katznelson's question. The paper presents it as an open question following its disproof of the higher-order analogue.

371807.title: The Thue list-number conjecture for the infinite path
371807.statement:
A graph coloring is **nonrepetitive** if the color sequence along every path contains no square. The **Thue-list number** of a graph is the least integer $k$ such that, whenever every vertex has a list of at least $k$ available colors, the graph has a nonrepetitive coloring choosing each vertex's color from its list.

**Thue list-number conjecture.** The Thue list number of the infinite path is $3$.

This is a list-coloring analogue of Thue's results on avoiding repetitions in words. The source presents it as a challenging conjecture and considers a word-theoretic reformulation; no resolution is given here.

371948.title: Existence conjecture for a projective-geometry triple-array family
371948.statement:
Let $q$ be a prime power. A triple array with parameters $(r,c,n)$ has $r=\frac{q^3-1}{q-1}$, $c=\frac{q^4-1}{q-1}$, and $n=\frac{(q^4-1)(q^3-1)}{(q^2-1)(q-1)}$.

**Existence conjecture.** For any prime power $q$, there is a $\left(\frac{q^3-1}{q-1},\frac{q^4-1}{q-1},\frac{(q^4-1)(q^3-1)}{(q^2-1)(q-1)}\right)$-triple array.

This conjecture asserts existence for the parameter family associated with the paper's projective-geometry construction. The supplied text gives no resolution or status evidence beyond the conjectural formulation.

372202.title: The characterization of locally interval graphs as circular-arc graphs
372202.statement:
Given a graph $G$ and a vertex $v$ of $G$, let $B_G(v,r/2)$ be the subgraph induced by vertices at distance at most $\lfloor r/2\rfloor$ from $v$, with edges $xy$ satisfying $d(v,x)+d(v,y)<r$. The graph $G$ is **$r$-locally interval** if every such ball is an interval graph. A graph is **circular-arc** if it has a region representation over a cycle in which every region is a path.

**Rz\k{a}\.{z}ewski's conjecture.** Locally interval graphs are exactly circular-arc graphs.

This conjecture proposes that being locally path-like, in the sense that all sufficiently specified local balls are interval graphs, is equivalent to admitting a region representation over a cycle. The source gives no resolution status.

372213.title: Superexponential chromatic evaluation spectrum at -1
372213.statement: For each integer $n\geq 1$, let $\mathsf{S}_n(-1)=\{P_G(-1):G\text{ is a simple graph on }n\text{ vertices}\}$. Since $|P_G(-1)|$ counts acyclic orientations of $G$, the spectrum can in principle have an upper bound as large as $|P_{K_n}(-1)|=n!$. **Superexponential spectrum conjecture.** The cardinality $|\mathsf{S}_n(-1)|$ is superexponential in $n$. This asks whether the distinct numbers of acyclic orientations, viewed through chromatic-polynomial evaluations, occur in superexponentially many values; the paper leaves the question open.

372320.title: Conjectured dominion formula for cycles
372320.statement:
Let $G$ be a cycle on $n\ge 3$ vertices. Its **dominion** is the invariant denoted by $\zeta(G)$. **Cycle dominion conjecture.** If $G$ is a cycle on $n\ge 3$ vertices, then

$$
\zeta(G)=\begin{cases} \frac{n^2+5n}{6}, & \text{if } n \equiv 1\pmod3 \\ n, & \text{if } n \equiv 2\pmod3. \end{cases}
$$

The cases $n\equiv 1,2\pmod3$ are presented as conjectural because the corresponding values are extrapolated from early recurring values using Lagrange interpolation; the case $n\equiv 0\pmod3$ was established separately in the preceding argument.
